findings.title: A breached boundary becomes forced re-entry
findings.claim: At فَسَقُوا۟, the peel-emergence branch can render deviation as breaking from a containing boundary; the repeated wish to exit then turns outward motion into a return into Fire.
findings.mechanism: The root-level peel image contacts the explicit أَن يَخْرُجُوا۟ and passive أُعِيدُوا۟ sequence, restarted by كُلَّمَا. The near-verbatim Fire-exit-return-taste scene in 22:22 supplies a wider action-pattern trigger that returns to this focus sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene becomes a structural reversal: an earlier boundary-crossing image is answered by a Fire from which each attempted emergence is converted into renewed enclosure.
findings.containment: The peel branch is an analogical root image, not a claim that فَسَقُوا۟ lexically means peeling here. The 22:22 connection corroborates the scene pattern only; target morphology is not supplied there. The focus's literal exit/return wording controls.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus-root support and the exact focus wording ground the contrast, while the peel mapping is analogical and the wider parallel lacks target morphology.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Taze hurma tanesi, kendisini saran kabuğun içinden dışarı çıkar.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus explicitly names an attempted خروج from Fire, and 22:22 repeats the Fire-exit-return pattern.
branch_activations.activation: The peel-emergence image meets a concrete exit attempt and its forced return, converting the moral label into a bounded boundary image.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Deviation is pictured as emergence from a containing boundary answered by failed emergence from Fire.
branch_activations.boundary: Analogical root image only; the ordinary moral force of فَسَقُوا۟ is not replaced.

findings.title: A refuge-form destination becomes an anti-refuge
findings.claim: The matched maʾwā designation in 32:19 and 32:20 preserves a destination of gathering but reverses its protective function: the garden is refuge for believers, while Fire is the destination assigned to the deniers.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier مَأْوَىٰهُمُ is paired with the positive garden-maʾwā of 32:19, then predicated of Fire. Wider uses name Fire itself as maʾwā (5:72), contrast it with the garden of refuge (53:15), and depict an enclosing Fire (18:29); these triggers return through the focus's maʾwā relation and invert shelter into inescapable endpoint.
findings.reader_payoff: The same destination grammar can carry opposed outcomes: refuge is not guaranteed by the word itself; the predicate and its enclosing force decide whether gathering protects or confines.
findings.containment: Fire remains the literal destination. “Anti-refuge” describes the reversal of shelter's expected function, not a claim that مأوى lexically means prison or that Fire protects.

epistemic.reason: The focus's paired maʾwā construction and explicit Fire predicate are direct; the wider refuge network supports a functional inversion that remains interpretive.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 32:19 supplies the positive garden-maʾwā pairing; 5:72 explicitly calls Fire a maʾwā; 53:15 names the garden of maʾwā; 18:29 supplies an enclosing Fire image.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's shelter/destination carrier contacts positive refuge scenes and the wider Fire destination, returning through its own Fire predicate.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: A refuge-form destination is functionally inverted into a place of confinement.
branch_activations.boundary: The root relation does not make Fire protective; the anti-refuge reading is a contextual reversal.

findings.title: Desire, exit and forced return form a loop
findings.claim: At each occasion signaled by كُلَّمَا, the wish to leave becomes an attempted boundary crossing and passive reinsertion; the next wish can begin, but its outcome is structurally fixed.
findings.mechanism: The focus orders أَرَادُوا۟, يَخْرُجُوا۟, and أُعِيدُوا۟ as desire → exit → forced return, with كُلَّمَا restarting the relation. The near-verbatim 22:22 scene gives a wider Fire-exit-return-taste counterpart that returns through those focus verbs.
findings.reader_payoff: Punishment is dynamic confinement rather than a static placement: intention remains visible, but every outward motion is redirected inward.
findings.containment: The repeated forced exit failure is explicit in the focus. Do not equate ع و د with moral رجوع; 22:22 supports the scene pattern only because its target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The core loop is explicit in the focus and independently captured by trusted evidence; the wider parallel corroborates the action pattern without importing morphology.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Agency appears as renewed wanting inside a cycle whose outcome is not chosen.
branch_activations.boundary: The wish itself is real; the reading concerns its repeated frustrated result.

findings.title: The denied revelation becomes bodily evidence
findings.claim: The accusation that the revelation was fabricated in 32:3 is answered at 32:20 by naming Fire as what they denied and commanding them to taste its punishment: discursive denial is carried into bodily experience rather than answered only with another argument.
findings.mechanism: The wider passage moves from what was sent down (32:2) through the fabrication allegation (32:3). In the focus, passive قِيلَ issues the command, the relative clause links Fire-punishment to what they denied, and ذُوقُوا۟ makes the denied object directly experienced. The 34:42 connection supplies a wider deny-Fire/taste counterpart.
findings.reader_payoff: The contradiction between denial and reality becomes the punishment's mechanism: a rejected report returns as an unavoidable bodily encounter, while the focus's Fire/light root image can make that encounter exposing as well as painful.
findings.containment: HFT context roots and word indices are attributed; the exact Arabic verifies surface contact, not target morphology. A weak 32:3 row says that ayah adds no specific consequence pattern, and the HFT live alternative is thematic denial repetition without a speaker-role mechanism. The light branch is analogical exposure, not a second lexical meaning of نار.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus evidence establishes denial followed by commanded tasting; the cross-ayah speaker-role reversal and light-as-exposure layer rely on attributed contextual traces and remain bounded.

findings.title: The return contrast has a temporal window
findings.claim: The compulsory spatial return in 32:20 is not every kind of return: 32:21 still describes lesser punishment as possibly prompting moral reorientation, while 32:29 removes benefit from late belief. Together they make the focus's loop a sign of closed agency, not a universal denial that return can ever be sought.
findings.mechanism: The wider corrective aim and later no-benefit limit meet the focus's passive أُعِيدُوا۟ and failed-exit act: the first marks a still-open interval for moral turning, and the latter its closure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish corrective consequence before an endpoint from futile movement after it; the attempted exit is spatial motion that cannot reopen the earlier moral option.
findings.containment: The moral رجوع in 32:21 and spatial إعادة in 32:20 are not one lexeme or one mechanism. 32:29 supplies a temporal limit, not additional detail about the focus's Fire scene.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk support explicitly names both contextual endpoints and their return to the focus; its broader synthesis remains legacy-unbound.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Ayrılınan bir şeye geri gelme ve başlangıçtan sonra aynı işe yeniden yönelme çekirdektir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 32:21 supplies a different, moral return as the hoped-for aim of lesser punishment; 32:29 says late belief yields no benefit.
branch_activations.activation: The same broad motion of returning is contrasted with a still-possible corrective turn and then a closed late endpoint.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's forced return belongs to the closed-agency phase of a wider moral window.
branch_activations.boundary: The 32:21 return belongs to a different root and must not be collapsed with the focus verb.

findings.title: Measured ascent frames a closed exit cycle
findings.claim: The ordered administration, ascent, and counted time in 32:5 can make the focus's repeated failed exit read as a counter-image to a measured, governed cosmic cycle: movement exists, but not as escape from Fire.
findings.mechanism: 32:5 joins administration with ascent and a measured day; the focus's كُلَّمَا totalizes desire and attempted exit while passive return intercepts each outward motion. This contrast redirects the scale of managed movement toward closed recurrence.
findings.reader_payoff: The cosmic movement frame highlights that motion alone does not guarantee personal egress; the Fire-bound cycle remains bounded.
findings.containment: This is exploratory: 32:5 may offer scale without an intentional return schedule. The proposed count-to-return branch is excluded because 32:5:17 has root ع د د, not the focus branch's root ع و د; no counted escape cycle is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is exact at the supplied context coordinates but legacy-unbound; the count link is rejected and the retained relation remains analogical.

findings.reader_payoff: The forced return is perceptible as the opposite of resurrection or restoration: the people move back, but not into a renewed life.
findings.containment: All context-root labels and indices remain attributed HFT nominations. The request in 32:12 is a plea, not guaranteed restoration, and the focus is not thereby a detailed account of resurrection logistics.

epistemic.reason: The exact contextual Arabic and focus sequence align with the attributed trace; the creation/death interpretation remains a bounded reader inference.
